answer: Yes. `share.gitBlobSha(text)` returns the git blob SHA-1 of `text` (as UTF-8), which is the same `hash` that `net.listURI` entries carry for GitHub (see `API/share.md`). The notes I found don't say it is safe for security. It's a SHA-1 change-detection hash, so use it to compare files and not for security.

API/share.md:18:Tells offline whether a page changed locally since its last pull or sync, as its `share.hash` tells, without reading the remote. Returns `{uri, mode, state}` where `state` is `unchanged`, `localChanged`, or `unknown` when the page has no `share.hash` to compare with. A `push` page is always `unchecked`: push keeps no `share.hash`, so only its remote can tell (see [[#share.check(names)]]). Remembered per page on its text, as views ask often.
API/share.md:21:Reads the remotes of the given pages and compares them with the local pages and their `share.hash`. Never prompts, connects, signs in or writes: a remote that needs a sign-in is reported as an error. Returns a table keyed by page name with `{uri, mode, state}` where `state` is one of:
API/share.md:24:* `localChanged`: only the local page changed since the `share.hash` (the remote still matches it).
API/share.md:25:* `remoteChanged`: only the remote changed (the page still matches its `share.hash`).
API/share.md:27:* `differs`: they differ, and there is no `share.hash` to tell which side changed. Always the case for `push`, which keeps none (a `share.hash` left on a push page by older versions is ignored).
API/share.md:58:Reads the remote and compares it with what each member would send, like [[#share.check(names)]]. Where the target has a [[#net.listURI: and net.deleteURI:|listing]], one listing is read, and a member whose entry has a `hash` is compared by its [[#share.gitBlobSha(text)|git blob SHA]] without reading it. Otherwise each member is read. Never prompts, connects, signs in or writes. Returns `{members, removed}`: `members` is keyed by page name with `{uri, state}`, `state` being `upToDate`, `missing`, `differs` or `error` (with the message in `error`), and `removed` lists the URIs of the listed files no member maps to (empty without a listing).
API/share.md:61:Publishes a collection, the same as `Share: Collection`: first prepares the root’s transport with [[#share.ensureTransport(uri)]] (which may ask to connect or sign in), so the members’ URIs are those of the root’s [[#share:target:<uri>|target]] even when the transport was set up just now. Then resolves the collection and transforms every member with the collection as the share set (afresh, so baked content is current) (see `members` at [[#share.transform(text, ctx)]]), lists the root (letting the provider sign in, `{signIn = true}`), writes the members whose text differs from the remote (by the listed `hash`, or else by reading the member’s remote, one that can’t be read is written) and offers the listed files no member maps to for removal with [[API/editor#editor.pickMany|editor.pickMany]], every item unticked. Only ticked files are deleted. Writes and deletes go in one call to a [[#share:writeBatch:<root>]] service when the root has one, and otherwise through `net.writeURI` and `net.deleteURI` one by one.
API/share.md:81:The decision behind the states of [[#share.check(names)]] and [[#share.checkCollection(name)]]: returns `missing`, `upToDate`, `localChanged`, `remoteChanged`, `bothChanged` or `differs`. `r.remote` is `nil` when the remote is missing, `{text = ...}` for its text (as `share.readRemote` returns it) or `{sha = ...}` for its [[#share.gitBlobSha(text)|git blob SHA]]. `r.outgoing` is what would be sent. `r.hash` (optional) is the page’s `share.hash`: without it a remote that isn’t `upToDate` `differs`. With it, a remote matching the hash means only the local side changed, an outgoing text matching it means only the remote changed, and neither means both. The hash is compared with `r.remote.text` only.
API/share.md:87:Returns the git blob SHA-1 of `text` (as UTF-8), the `hash` that `net.listURI` entries carry for GitHub, so a file can be compared without reading it.

Nothing is written when the page already equals the remote, or the remote hasn’t changed since it was installed (it matches the page’s `share.hash`), so local edits stay until there is something new. When there is, local edits (the page no longer matches its `share.hash`) are only replaced once the user confirms. Without a `share.hash` the remote replaces the page without asking. After every pull or sync that agrees on a text with the remote, including one where both sides were already equal, it is set to that text’s hash (only the frontmatter changes when the text is already the page’s). Space sync carries it to your other devices with the page. `push` never edits the page: it compares with the remote instead.

For Std pages that memoize per key (such as `share.status`): returns `memo(key, inputs, compute)`, which returns the result kept for `key` while `inputs` (a table of values, compared with `==`) are unchanged, and otherwise calls `compute()` and keeps its result. `copy(result)`, when given, makes what each call returns, so callers changing it leave the memo alone.

## share.gitBlobSha(text)
Returns the git blob SHA-1 of `text` (as UTF-8), the `hash` that `net.listURI` entries carry for GitHub, so a file can be compared without reading it.

## share.prepare(name, text)
Returns `{m, mode, outgoing}` for a page: its `share` frontmatter table, the mode (`push` when unset), and the text that goes to the remote. For `push` that is `text` run through [[#share.transform(text, ctx)]] with the steps resolved for the target of the URI. For `pull` and `sync` it is `text` with only the `share.*` keys removed. Errors with `Not configured` when the page has no `share.uri`.
